# Building Raindrops on GitLab (no Termux)

Pipeline file: `.gitlab-ci.yml` (V1.9.8). Jobs: `check` (lint, can never block the build), `build-apk` (every branch push, or Build > Pipelines > Run pipeline), `signing-key` (manual, optional).
Output: Build > Pipelines > open the pipeline > `build-apk` > Download artifacts > `raindrops.apk`. `gradle-build.log` and `prep.log` are saved too, even when the build fails.

## Files that must be in the repo (everything else is generated by the pipeline)
`.gitlab-ci.yml`, `package.json`, `capacitor.config.json`, `prep-android.sh`, `www/`, `native/` (including `native/optional/RenderGuard.java`), `android-res/`, `scripts/newpipe.version`, `.gitignore`.
Do NOT upload `node_modules/`, `android/build/`, `*.apk`. The `android/` folder is created by `npx cap add android` inside CI; if you already have one committed, extract this zip over it and keep it.
Extract the zip OVER the repo (keep your other files), commit, push.

## If the pipeline fails
Open the failed job. Scroll to the bottom: "last 40 lines of the Gradle log" is printed there. Copy the red lines and paste them to me. If it died earlier, open `prep.log` from the artifacts. The first lines of the job show the Java and Node versions that were used.

## Make updates install over the old app (important)
Android refuses an update signed with a different key (the install fails, you keep the OLD app and the OLD icon).
- Option A, keep your current library: if your installed app was built in Termux, its key is `~/.android/debug.keystore`. Run once: `base64 -w0 ~/.android/debug.keystore` and save the output as the masked CI/CD variable `DEBUG_KEYSTORE_B64`.
- Option B, clean permanent key: run the manual `signing-key` job, download `raindrops-signing-vars.txt`, paste the four lines as masked variables. This is a NEW key, so uninstall the old app once first (songs saved inside the old app are lost, export recordings first).

## If YouTube breaks later
Set `NEWPIPE_VERSION` (example `v0.26.5`) in Settings > CI/CD > Variables, or edit `scripts/newpipe.version`. prep-android.sh checks the version exists on JitPack and falls back to older tags if it does not (see prep.log, line "NewPipe version in use").

## In the app
Record tab > Fix + diagnose > Check. It tests the YouTube plugin, Deezer, Audius, lyrics and Wikipedia and shows the exact error. Copy report puts it on the clipboard.
